patch.objective: Relational databases, data modelling and SQL: tables linked by primary and foreign keys, and queries that join them to pull data on many patients
secondaryObjectives: Structured versus unstructured clinical data, and why free-text notes are harder to search, count and reuse

sources.cite: AMIA Accreditation Committee, foundational domains for master's-level health informatics education (CAHIIM HI master's curriculum requirements PDF)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch. F2 (Information Science and Technology) is the working knowledge of data, information and systems the field builds on; the MSHI course places relational databases and SQL there. The case is a retail list query: the decision it teaches (a NULL in a NOT IN list makes the filter unknown for every row, so use NOT EXISTS and prove the list with an independent count) is the same for any query across patient tables, such as patients without a visit since a date.

sources.cite: PostgreSQL 16 documentation, 9.23 Subquery Expressions (9.23.3 NOT IN)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch 2026-11-16 (PostgreSQL 16.16 documentation). Relevant text: 'Note that if the left-hand expression yields null, or if there are no equal right-hand values and at least one right-hand row yields null, the result of the NOT IN construct will be null, not true. This is in accordance with SQL's normal rules for Boolean combinations of null values.' The page documents EXISTS (9.23.1); NOT EXISTS is its negation, and the summary did not quote a NOT EXISTS paragraph. A WHERE clause keeps only rows whose condition is true, so a null NOT IN drops every row.
